A log fold change and a Wald-usable standard error for eSVD-DE: what the autoresearch run nov11 kept, and why

Kevin Z. Lin (drafted by Claude)

2026-11-11

Overview

This document is built from the design memo of the loop (MEMO_claude.md), the record of the bank as built (BANK.md), the run report that the autoresearch protocol requires (RUN_nov11_claude.md), and the tables of the run (csv/RUN_nov11/). It follows the sections of that protocol’s run report, and every number in its prose is read from those tables.

The question. Version 1.2.0 of eSVD2 reports a log fold change and a standard error whose ratio is not a usable Wald statistic. The autoresearch loop searched for a rule that reports, from one fitted cohort, a log2 fold change that is unbiased at every effect size and a standard error that is the sampling SD of that log fold change. The run nov11 edited one file (report_rule_claude.R) over 38 experiments, each scored on a fixed bank of simulated cohorts.

The document argues five things.

  1. The kept rule, donor_wls, is a donor-level weighted regression of log pseudobulk ratios with a moderated residual variance (Section 1.3).
  2. It scores -0.0769 on the dev split and -0.0712 on the held-out test split, against 0.0097 and 0.0178 for the baseline raw_null, and the dev gain carried to test in full (Section 3).
  3. Three of the 15 kept commits carry 87% of the dev gain (Section 4).
  4. Two commits that passed the keep rule were withdrawn, because their standard error followed the estimated log fold change, which the score rewards and the gate does not detect (Section 5).
  5. Quantities of the fit that are estimated at the level of cells (the case-control coefficient, the low-rank term, the nuisance rate) did not help (Section 6).

How to read. A green box closes each results section with what that section changes. The blue box describes the simulated bank once, and a grey box opens each section that reuses it. The orange box in Section 8 is the procedure. A reader of the boxes alone gets the argument.

1 Definitions

1.1 Notation

A cohort has cells \(c\), genes \(g = 1, \dots, p\) and donors \(d = 1, \dots, n\), of which \(n_1\) are cases and \(n_0\) controls. \(A_{cg}\) is the count of cell \(c\) and gene \(g\). \(\ell_{cg}\) is the fitted library size of eSVD-DE, which holds every fitted covariate effect except the case-control one, the gene intercept included. \(\beta_g\) is the true log2 fold change of gene \(g\), and a rule reports the pair \((\widehat\beta_g, s_g)\) in log2 units.

A rule is a function report_lfc_se(view). The list view holds what a user has after eSVD(): the counts, the design matrix, the donor and the arm of each cell, the fitted library, the posterior mean and variance, and the nuisance rate.

Name in the tables Rule Reads Defined in
raw_null log ratio of the arms’ mean donor ratios, delta-method SE, shifted and rescaled by the empirical null counts, fitted library 1.2
donor_wls arm coefficient of a donor-level weighted regression of log pseudobulk ratios, moderated residual variance, constant shift counts, fitted library, design 1.3
gap_trend donor_wls as of experiment 27, with the variance moderated toward a trend in the arithmetic-geometric gap of the donor ratios counts, fitted library, design 5
deseq2 DESeq2 on donor pseudobulk counts, stored with the bank as a reference counts 1.4

1.2 The baseline: raw_null

With \(m_{dg}\) the mean of \(A_{cg} / \ell_{cg}\) over the cells of donor \(d\), \(M_{1g}, M_{0g}\) the arm means of \(m_{dg}\) and \(V_{1g}, V_{0g}\) the sample variances of \(m_{dg}\) within each arm,

\[\widehat\beta^{\,\text{raw}}_g = \log_2\frac{M_{1g}}{M_{0g}}, \qquad s^{\text{raw}}_g = \frac{1}{\ln 2}\sqrt{\frac{V_{1g}}{n_1 M_{1g}^2} + \frac{V_{0g}}{n_0 M_{0g}^2}}.\]

With \((\delta_0, \sigma_0)\) the mean and SD of the empirical null fitted to \(\widehat\beta^{\,\text{raw}}_g / s^{\text{raw}}_g\) over the genes, raw_null reports \((\widehat\beta^{\,\text{raw}}_g - \delta_0 s^{\text{raw}}_g,\; \sigma_0 s^{\text{raw}}_g)\).

1.3 The kept rule: donor_wls

  1. Donor summary. With \(y_{dg} = \sum_{c \in d} A_{cg}\) and \(L_{dg} = \sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg}\), \[l_{dg} = \log\frac{y_{dg} + 1/2}{L_{dg}}.\]
  2. Design. \(D\) is the \(n \times q\) donor-level matrix whose columns are the intercept, the arm indicator, and every column of the fit’s design that is constant within donors, reduced to full rank.
  3. Donor offsets. With \(r_{dg}\) the residuals of the least-squares regression of \(l_{\cdot g}\) on \(D\), the offset of donor \(d\) is \(o_d = \text{median}_g\, r_{dg}\), and \(l_{dg} \leftarrow l_{dg} - o_d\). The regression is repeated, which gives the fitted values \(f_{dg}\) and the residuals \(r_{dg}\).
  4. Precision weights. With \(\mu_{dg} = L_{dg}\, e^{f_{dg}}\) the expected count, the two constants of \[\text{Var}(l_{dg}) = \tau^2 + \frac{\phi}{\mu_{dg}}\] are fitted by least squares of \(r_{dg}^2\, n / (n - q)\) on \(1 / \mu_{dg}\) over all donors and genes, each floored at 0, and \(w_{dg} = 1 / (\tau^2 + \phi / \mu_{dg})\).
  5. Weighted regression. With \(W_g = \text{diag}(w_{\cdot g})\), \[\widehat\theta_g = (D^\top W_g D)^{-1} D^\top W_g\, l_{\cdot g}, \qquad a_g = \big[(D^\top W_g D)^{-1}\big]_{\text{arm}}, \qquad S_g = \frac{1}{n - q}\sum_d w_{dg}\,(l_{dg} - D_d^\top \widehat\theta_g)^2 .\] The vector \(\widehat\theta_g\) has one entry per column of \(D\), and \(\widehat\theta_{g,\text{arm}}\) is its entry for the arm indicator: the difference between cases and controls in the mean of \(l_{dg}\), at equal donor-level covariates, in natural-log units. It is computed by this regression and is not eSVD-DE’s fitted case-control coefficient \(\widehat z_{g,\text{cc}}\) (Section 1.3.1).
  6. Moderated variance. A smoothing spline \(t(\cdot)\), with its smoothness chosen by generalized cross-validation, is fitted to \(\log S_g\) against \(x_g = \tfrac1n \sum_d f_{dg}\). With \(\nu = n - q\), \(\psi\) the digamma function and \(\psi'\) the trigamma function, the prior degrees of freedom \(\nu_0\) solve \[\psi'(\nu_0 / 2) = \text{mean}_g\,\{\log S_g - t(x_g)\}^2 - \psi'(\nu / 2),\] the prior variance is \(\log S_{0g} = t(x_g) - \psi(\nu/2) + \log(\nu/2) + \psi(\nu_0/2) - \log(\nu_0/2)\), and \[\widetilde S_g = \frac{\nu_0 S_{0g} + \nu S_g}{\nu_0 + \nu}.\] When the right-hand side of the equation for \(\nu_0\) is not positive, \(\nu_0 = \infty\) and \(\widetilde S_g = \exp\{t(x_g) - \psi(\nu/2) + \log(\nu/2)\}\).
  7. The pair before centring. \[\widehat\beta^{\,0}_g = \frac{\widehat\theta_{g,\text{arm}}}{\ln 2}, \qquad s_g = \frac{\sqrt{\widetilde S_g\, a_g}}{\ln 2}.\]
  8. Centring. With \(\delta_0\) the mean of the empirical null fitted by eSVD2::multtest() to \(z_g = \widehat\beta^{\,0}_g / s_g\), \[\widehat\beta_g = \widehat\beta^{\,0}_g - \delta_0 \cdot \text{median}_g\, s_g .\] The rule reports \((\widehat\beta_g, s_g)\), and the SD of the empirical null is not used.

Four things changed against raw_null. The donor summary is a ratio of sums on the log scale. The estimator is a regression that adjusts again for the donor-level covariates and weights donors by their precision. The variance is pooled over the arms and moderated across genes, with the cost of the covariates in \(a_g\) and in \(\nu\). The centring is one constant per cohort, with no rescaling of the SE. Steps 5 to 7 are the moderated statistic of limma on precision weights in the manner of voom (smyth2004linear, law2014voom), applied to eSVD-DE’s fitted library in place of a normalized library size.

1.3.1 Where the eSVD-DE fit enters

eSVD-DE fits, for cell \(c\) and gene \(g\), the mean count

\[\widehat{\mathbb{E}}[A_{cg}] = \exp\Big(\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g + \sum_{k} \widehat z_{gk}\, C_{ck}\Big) = \underbrace{\exp\Big(\sum_{k \ne \text{cc}} \widehat z_{gk}\, C_{ck}\Big)}_{\ell_{cg}} \cdot \exp\big(\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g + \widehat z_{g,\text{cc}}\, C_{c,\text{cc}}\big),\]

where \(C_{ck}\) is covariate \(k\) of cell \(c\) (the intercept, the log of the cell’s total count, the case-control indicator cc, and any others), \(\widehat z_{gk}\) is the fitted coefficient of gene \(g\) on covariate \(k\), and \(\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g\) is the fitted low-rank term. The fitted library \(\ell_{cg}\) is the first factor, floored at 0.1 as compute_posterior() floors it. It is the count the fit expects from cell \(c\) for gene \(g\) at the cell’s depth and covariates, before the arm and the low-rank term act.

donor_wls uses one fitted quantity, \(\ell_{cg}\), and uses it in two steps, both times summed over the cells of a donor, \(L_{dg} = \sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg}\).

  • Step 1, as the denominator of the donor summary. The count of a cell has mean \(\ell_{cg} \lambda_{cg}\), with \(\lambda_{cg}\) the cell’s expression relative to its library, so \[\mathbb{E}[y_{dg}] = \sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg}\, \lambda_{cg} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{y_{dg}}{L_{dg}} \approx \frac{\sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg}\, \lambda_{cg}}{\sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg}},\] the library-weighted mean of \(\lambda_{cg}\) over the donor’s cells. The response of the regression, \(l_{dg} = \log\{(y_{dg} + 1/2) / L_{dg}\}\), is the log of that ratio. This step is where the fit’s adjustment for depth and for every covariate other than the arm, cell by cell and gene by gene, enters the log fold change. A pseudobulk method divides by one normalized library size per donor in this place.
  • Step 4, in the expected count that sets the weights. The expected count \(\mu_{dg} = L_{dg}\, e^{f_{dg}}\) multiplies the summed fitted library by the donor regression’s own fitted ratio, and the weight \(w_{dg} = 1 / (\tau^2 + \phi / \mu_{dg})\) falls as \(\mu_{dg}\) falls. Through the weights \(L_{dg}\) also enters \(\widehat\theta_g\), \(a_g\) and \(S_g\) of step 5.

Every later quantity inherits the fit through these two steps only. The \(f_{dg}\) of steps 3, 4 and 6 are fitted values of the donor-level regression of \(l_{dg}\) on \(D\). They are computed by the rule and are not values of the eSVD-DE fit.

Quantity of the eSVD-DE fit Used by donor_wls Where
fitted library \(\ell_{cg}\), from \(\widehat z_{gk}\) for \(k \ne \text{cc}\) yes steps 1 and 4, as \(L_{dg}\)
design matrix \(C\) (built by format_covariates(), not fitted) yes step 2, its columns that are constant within donors
case-control coefficient \(\widehat z_{g,\text{cc}}\) no the arm effect is estimated again in step 5
low-rank term \(\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g\) no
nuisance rate \(\widehat\gamma_g\) and its capped status no
posterior mean and variance of each cell and gene no

The donor-level covariates therefore act twice: once inside \(\ell_{cg}\), where the fit removes their effect cell by cell, and once in \(D\), where the regression of step 5 removes what is left of them between donors and charges the arm coefficient for it through \(a_g\) and \(\nu\). The call to eSVD2::multtest() in step 8 uses a function of the package on the rule’s own \(z_g\) and reads nothing of the fit. Experiments 11, 18 and 24 tried the three unused fitted quantities in turn, and each lost (Section 6).

1.3.2 The logic of the estimate, and what remains of eSVD-DE

The short answer. donor_wls computes its log fold change and its SE from the counts and the fitted library alone. The embedding, the fitted case-control coefficient, the nuisance rate, the posterior mean and the posterior variance do not enter either number. The rule is close to a limma-voom analysis of donor pseudobulk counts in which eSVD-DE’s fitted library replaces the normalized library size.

The log fold change. The target is the log2 ratio of mean expression between the arms at equal depth and equal covariates, and the unit that is replicated is the donor. The rule therefore reduces each donor to one number per gene, \(l_{dg}\), the log of the donor’s expression relative to its fitted library (Section 1.3.1), and compares the arms on that scale. With no donor-level covariate and equal weights, step 5 reduces to a difference of two averages,

\[\widehat\theta_{g,\text{arm}} = \frac{1}{n_1}\sum_{d\,\in\,\text{cases}} l_{dg} \;-\; \frac{1}{n_0}\sum_{d\,\in\,\text{controls}} l_{dg}, \qquad \widehat\beta^{\,0}_g = \frac{\widehat\theta_{g,\text{arm}}}{\ln 2}.\]

The regression generalizes this difference in two ways: the columns of \(D\) for sex and age hold those covariates equal between the arms, and the weights \(w_{dg}\) let a donor with few counts for the gene count for less.

The standard error. If \(l_{dg}\) has variance \(\sigma_g^2 / w_{dg}\) around its regression line, independently over donors, then

\[\text{Var}\big(\widehat\theta_{g,\text{arm}}\big) = \sigma_g^2\, a_g, \qquad a_g = \big[(D^\top W_g D)^{-1}\big]_{\text{arm}} \;\overset{\text{no covariates, equal weights}}{=}\; \frac{1}{n_1} + \frac{1}{n_0}.\]

The factor \(a_g\) is known from the design, and it grows when sex or age is unbalanced between the arms. The variance \(\sigma_g^2\) is the spread of the donors around the line, donor-to-donor biological variation plus the sampling noise of the counts, and \(S_g\) estimates it from \(n - q\) degrees of freedom. With 10 donors that estimate is too noisy to use gene by gene, so step 6 replaces it by \(\widetilde S_g\), a weighted average of \(S_g\) and the value that genes of similar expression have. The SE is \(\sqrt{\widetilde S_g\, a_g} / \ln 2\). It is a between-donor SE, and no within-donor or posterior variance is added to it.

Why the other fitted quantities are not used. Each was tried, in the exploration of 2026-11-07 or in this run.

Fitted quantity What happened when it was used Why
posterior mean the between-donor SE of posterior donor means was 0.65 to 0.73 times the SD of the log fold change over replicate cohorts (exploration) the posterior mean of a cell is \(w\, A_{cg} / \ell_{cg} + (1 - w) \times \text{fit}\), with \(w = \ell_{cg} / (\ell_{cg} + \widehat\gamma_g)\), so it pulls donors toward the fit and toward each other, and their spread understates the noise by about \(w\)
posterior variance as the SE of version 1.2.0, 3.4 to 5 times that SD (exploration); as a within-donor term added to the between-donor variance, kept at experiment 8 and removed at experiment 15 it describes the uncertainty of a cell’s expression given the fit, and the error of the log fold change is dominated by which donors were sampled
case-control coefficient \(\widehat z_{g,\text{cc}}\) experiment 11, worse by 0.072 nats it is fitted over cells, so a donor with many cells counts for more, and experiment 10 shows that weighting donors by cell count alone costs 0.056 nats
embedding \(\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g\) experiment 18, worse by 0.023 nats in a cohort of 10 to 40 donors the low-rank term absorbs part of the donor effects, so dividing by it removes variation that the error of the log fold change still contains
nuisance rate \(\widehat\gamma_g\) experiments 24 and 35, worse by 0.006 and 0.0004 nats the gene’s level already predicts its variance, and the rate is capped for part of the genes

The baseline raw_null had already dropped the posterior mean and variance for the first two reasons, before the run began. The run then found no fitted quantity worth adding back.

What the run does not show. Two limits bear on how far this result reaches.

  • The run did not score donor_wls with a plain library size (the cell’s total count) in place of \(\ell_{cg}\). The share of the 0.054 nats over deseq2 that the fitted library contributes, as opposed to the weights and the moderation, is therefore not measured.
  • The bank draws each cell’s embedding independently of its donor and its arm, so the low-rank term has no difference in cell state between cases and controls to remove. A cohort in which cell state is confounded with the arm is the setting where the embedding is expected to matter, and the bank does not contain it.

The p-value. The p-value was not on trial, and nothing in the package changed. Two p-values exist after this run, and they use the fit differently.

Statistic Computed by Uses of the eSVD-DE fit
the package’s p-value compute_test_statistic() and compute_pvalue(), unchanged posterior mean and posterior variance of every cell, hence the embedding, every coefficient and the nuisance rate; then the empirical null
the Wald statistic \(\widehat\beta_g / s_g\) of donor_wls report_lfc_se() the fitted library only

A user who reports the log fold change and SE of donor_wls beside the package’s p-value reports two analyses of the same counts, and the two can disagree on a gene. Whether compute_log_fold_change() should adopt donor_wls, and whether the p-value should then follow it, are decisions for Section 8.

The implementation is RULE_nov11_claude.R, which mirrors commit 5df592c and needs no other file of the project. Its code follows.

# The reporting rule kept by the autoresearch run `autoresearch_lfcse/nov11`:
# a log2 fold change and its standard error from one fitted eSVD-DE cohort.
# Drafted by Claude for Kevin Z. Lin, 2026-11-11.
#
# Mirrors commit 5df592c of `autoresearch_lfcse/report_rule_claude.R` (the
# code is identical; this header and one comment are rewritten).
# Score: Gaussian negative log-likelihood of the true log2 fold change,
# nats per gene, lower is better, on the bank `lfcse-bank-1`.
#              baseline `raw_null`    this rule
#   dev            0.0097              -0.0769
#   test           0.0178              -0.0712
#
# Use: `res_df <- report_lfc_se(view)`, where `view` is a list holding what
# a user has after `eSVD()` with `bool_diet = FALSE`. The rule reads
#   view$dat               counts, cells x genes, with gene names as colnames
#   view$library_mat       fitted library size per cell and gene (every
#                          covariate but the case-control one, the intercept
#                          included)
#   view$covariates        the design matrix of the fit, cells x covariates
#   view$individual_vec    donor of each cell
#   view$case_control_vec  arm of each cell, 1 for cases and 0 for controls
# and returns a data frame with one row per gene and columns `gene`,
# `log2fc`, `se`. It needs the packages `stats` and `eSVD2` (for
# `eSVD2::multtest()`, which calls `locfdr`).
#
# The rule, in order.
# 1. Donor summary. For donor d and gene g, y_dg is the donor's summed
#    count and L_dg its summed fitted library; l_dg = log((y_dg + 1/2) /
#    L_dg).
# 2. Donor-level design D: intercept, arm, and every covariate that is
#    constant within donors.
# 3. Least squares of l on D; each donor's median residual over genes is
#    subtracted from its row of l (an offset common to all genes), and the
#    least squares is repeated.
# 4. Precision weights w_dg = 1 / (tau^2 + phi / mu_dg), with mu_dg the
#    fitted expected count and (tau^2, phi) fitted by least squares to the
#    squared residuals over all donors and genes.
# 5. Weighted least squares gene by gene: lfc_g = (arm coefficient) / ln 2,
#    a_g = [(D' W_g D)^-1]_arm, and the weighted residual variance S_g on
#    n - rank(D) degrees of freedom.
# 6. S_g is moderated toward its trend in the gene's mean fitted value
#    (`.moderate_variance()`, Smyth 2004): se_g = sqrt(S~_g a_g) / ln 2.
# 7. Centring: the empirical null's mean d0 of z = lfc / se
#    (`eSVD2::multtest()`); the rule reports (lfc - d0 * median(se), se).

# Inverse of the trigamma function by Newton's method on its reciprocal
# (Smyth 2004, appendix); the start 0.5 + 1 / x is exact in both limits.
.trigamma_inverse <- function(x_val){
  y_val <- 0.5 + 1 / x_val
  for(iter in seq_len(50)){
    tri <- trigamma(y_val)
    step <- tri * (1 - tri / x_val) / psigamma(y_val, deriv = 2)
    y_val <- y_val + step
    # Relative step below single precision: converged.
    if(-step / y_val < 1e-8) break
  }
  y_val
}

# Moderate per-gene variances `var_vec`, each with `df` degrees of
# freedom, toward their trend in `covariate_vec` (Smyth 2004). On the log
# scale a scaled chi-square variance has mean log(s0^2) + digamma(df / 2) -
# log(df / 2) and variance trigamma(df / 2); the trend is a smoothing
# spline (smoothness by generalized cross-validation), and the excess of
# the residual variance over trigamma(df / 2) gives the prior degrees of
# freedom d0 through trigamma(d0 / 2). The moderated variance is
# (d0 * s0^2 + df * var) / (d0 + df).
.moderate_variance <- function(var_vec, df, covariate_vec){
  idx <- which(is.finite(var_vec) & var_vec > 0 & is.finite(covariate_vec))
  log_vec <- log(var_vec[idx])
  spline_fit <- stats::smooth.spline(x = covariate_vec[idx], y = log_vec)
  trend_vec <- stats::predict(spline_fit, x = covariate_vec)$y
  excess <- mean((log_vec - trend_vec[idx])^2) - trigamma(df / 2)
  if(excess <= 0){
    # No spread beyond sampling noise: every gene takes the trend.
    return(exp(trend_vec - digamma(df / 2) + log(df / 2)))
  }
  prior_df <- 2 * .trigamma_inverse(excess)
  prior_vec <- exp(trend_vec - digamma(df / 2) + log(df / 2) +
                     digamma(prior_df / 2) - log(prior_df / 2))
  (prior_df * prior_vec + df * var_vec) / (prior_df + df)
}

# The donor-level design: intercept, arm, and every column of `covariates`
# that is constant within donors (sex, age). The fitted library removes
# those covariates cell by cell; the donor-level regression removes what
# is left of them between donors and charges the arm coefficient for it.
.donor_design <- function(covariates, individual_vec, arm_vec, donor_vec){
  individual_chr <- as.character(individual_vec)
  first_idx <- match(donor_vec, individual_chr)
  bool_donor_level <- apply(covariates, 2, function(col_vec){
    all(col_vec == col_vec[first_idx][match(individual_chr, donor_vec)])
  })
  design_mat <- cbind(1, arm_vec,
                      covariates[first_idx, bool_donor_level, drop = FALSE])
  qr_res <- qr(design_mat)
  # Columns 1 and 2 (intercept, arm) are pivoted first, so the constant
  # and arm columns of `covariates` itself drop out as redundant.
  design_mat[, qr_res$pivot[seq_len(qr_res$rank)], drop = FALSE]
}

.arm_of_donor <- function(case_control_vec, individual_vec, donor_vec){
  case_control_vec[match(donor_vec, as.character(individual_vec))]
}

report_lfc_se <- function(view){
  # Donor summary: the ratio of sums, sum of counts over sum of fitted
  # library sizes, which weights each cell by its depth.
  individual_chr <- as.character(view$individual_vec)
  count_mat <- rowsum(view$dat, group = individual_chr)
  library_sum_mat <- rowsum(view$library_mat, group = individual_chr)
  mean_mat <- count_mat / library_sum_mat
  # Half a count keeps the logarithm of a donor with no count finite (the
  # continuity correction of a Poisson count).
  log_mat <- log((count_mat + 0.5) / library_sum_mat)
  donor_vec <- rownames(mean_mat)
  arm_vec <- .arm_of_donor(case_control_vec = view$case_control_vec,
                           individual_vec = view$individual_vec,
                           donor_vec = donor_vec)

  # Least squares of the log donor means on the donor-level design.
  design_mat <- .donor_design(covariates = view$covariates,
                              individual_vec = view$individual_vec,
                              arm_vec = arm_vec, donor_vec = donor_vec)
  fit_mat <- design_mat %*% solve(crossprod(design_mat),
                                  crossprod(design_mat, log_mat))
  # A donor's offset common to all genes (depth the library missed): the
  # median over genes of its residuals, removed before the variance is
  # estimated. The arm's share of such offsets is what the centring removes
  # from the logFC, so it does not belong in the SE either.
  offset_vec <- apply(log_mat - fit_mat, 1, stats::median)
  log_mat <- log_mat - offset_vec
  fit_mat <- design_mat %*% solve(crossprod(design_mat),
                                  crossprod(design_mat, log_mat))
  residual_df <- nrow(design_mat) - ncol(design_mat)
  # Precision weights from a two-part variance. A log donor mean varies by
  # a donor term common to all observations plus a sampling term inversely
  # proportional to the donor's expected count mu: variance = tau^2 +
  # phi / mu. The two constants are fitted by least squares to the squared
  # residuals (rescaled to be unbiased) over all donors and genes, and an
  # observation gets the weight 1 / (tau^2 + phi / mu), so that a donor
  # with few counts for a gene counts for less.
  inverse_count_vec <- as.numeric(exp(-(fit_mat + log(library_sum_mat))))
  squared_vec <- as.numeric((log_mat - fit_mat)^2) *
    nrow(design_mat) / residual_df
  slope <- stats::cov(squared_vec, inverse_count_vec) /
    stats::var(inverse_count_vec)
  variance_coef <- c(mean(squared_vec) - slope * mean(inverse_count_vec),
                     slope)
  # Neither part of a variance can be negative.
  variance_coef <- pmax(variance_coef, 0)
  weight_mat <- matrix(1 / (variance_coef[1] +
                              variance_coef[2] * inverse_count_vec),
                       nrow = nrow(fit_mat))

  # Weighted least squares, gene by gene.
  num_genes <- ncol(log_mat)
  lfc_vec <- numeric(num_genes)
  arm_var_vec <- numeric(num_genes)
  residual_var <- numeric(num_genes)
  for(j in seq_len(num_genes)){
    weighted_design <- design_mat * weight_mat[, j]
    gram_inv_mat <- solve(crossprod(design_mat, weighted_design))
    coef_vec <- gram_inv_mat %*% crossprod(weighted_design, log_mat[, j])
    lfc_vec[j] <- coef_vec[2] / log(2)
    arm_var_vec[j] <- gram_inv_mat[2, 2]
    residual_var[j] <- sum(weight_mat[, j] *
                             (log_mat[, j] - design_mat %*% coef_vec)^2) /
      residual_df
  }
  between_vec <- arm_var_vec *
    .moderate_variance(var_vec = residual_var, df = residual_df,
                       # The fitted values' mean over donors: the gene's
                       # level relative to the fitted library. The arm
                       # effect enters it only at second order, so the SE
                       # does not follow the estimated logFC.
                       covariate_vec = colMeans(fit_mat))

  se_vec <- sqrt(between_vec) / log(2)

  z_vec <- lfc_vec / se_vec
  # `multtest()` warns when locfdr falls back on its cruder estimators; the
  # estimate is still used.
  null_res <- suppressWarnings(eSVD2::multtest(z_vec[is.finite(z_vec)]))

  data.frame(gene = colnames(view$dat),
             log2fc = lfc_vec - null_res$null_mean * stats::median(se_vec),
             se = se_vec,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

1.4 The score, the gate and the reference

The score of one fitted cohort is the Gaussian negative log-likelihood of the truth under the reported pair, in nats per gene,

\[\text{NLL} = \frac{1}{p}\sum_{g=1}^{p}\left[\tfrac12 \log\!\left(2\pi s_g^2\right) + \frac{(\widehat\beta_g - \beta_g)^2}{2 s_g^2}\right],\]

and lower is better. One example of the bank is a pair of cohorts, the score of an example is the mean of its two cohorts’ NLL, and the score of a rule is the mean over the examples of a split. In expectation the NLL of a gene is smallest when \(s_g^2\) equals the mean squared error of \(\widehat\beta_g\), so it charges an SE that is too large, an SE that is too small, a biased log fold change and a noisy one in the same unit.

A proper score rewards shrinkage toward zero wherever the truth is sparse. The gate therefore requires slope_weak, the slope of the reported log fold change on the truth over the weak genes (\(0 < |\beta_g| < 0.5\)), to lie in \([0.9, 1.1]\), and a commit that fails the gate is not kept.

A commit is kept when its paired gain over the best commit so far is positive and at least one paired standard error over the 144 dev examples. deseq2 is scored with the same formula on the pair that DESeq2 reports from donor pseudobulk counts, and the line score_vs_deseq2 is a rule’s score minus that reference.

2 The run

Branch autoresearch_lfcse/nov11, cut from 2026-11-07_std at 89ff8f8
Budget agreed at setup 40 experiments or 4 hours, with 8 cores for a scoring
Experiments run 38, from 2026-11-12T01:22:22Z to 2026-11-12T01:51:16Z
By status 15 kept, 2 kept and then withdrawn, 21 discarded
Wall-clock per scoring 16 to 19 seconds
Best commit 5df592c (experiment 37)

What stopped the run. The run was stopped by a decision at experiment 38, two short of the budget. The 7 commits kept after experiment 13 moved the dev score by 0.0042 nats in total, and the ideas left were weaker than the ones just discarded.

One departure from the protocol. Experiments 28 and 29 (da743dc, b3fc556) passed the keep rule and were withdrawn afterwards (Section 5). The branch was reset to the previous kept commit 1de04e6, the best-score files were rebuilt from a fresh scoring of that commit, and the two commits are preserved on the branch autoresearch_lfcse/nov11-gap-invalid. The protocol has no such step, so the withdrawal is Kevin’s to confirm.

Two experiments crashed on coding errors (a formula interface and a string that the scorer’s tripwire refuses). Both were fixed and amended before they were logged, so the log has no crash row.

The bank lfcse-bank-1 holds 144 dev and 144 test examples. An example is a pair of cohorts of 600 genes whose counts follow the eSVD model at rank 3, with donor random effects on the log scale, and each cohort is fitted end to end by eSVD2 1.2.0. The case-control effects of the two cohorts are correlated at 0.8 with a size ratio of 2. Six factors are crossed, one example per cell and split: the number of donors (10, 20, 40, half per arm), the cells per donor (50 for every donor, or unequal from 30 to 600), the range of the true Gamma rate (narrow, wide), the effects (sparse: 10% of genes nonzero; sparse_up: the same sizes, all positive; dense: every gene nonzero), the covariates (none, or donor-level sex and age with sex imbalanced 60/40 between the arms), and the donor SD (0.2, 0.5, the quartiles estimated on the Velmeshev cohort). Both arms share the donor SD. The truth of an example is the generator’s case-control coefficient in log2 units. BANK.md records the bank as built.

Three commits carry 87% of the dev gain of 0.0866 nats.

  • The moderation (experiment 5, 0.045 nats). A variance estimated from 5 to 20 donors per arm is stabilized by the other genes’ variances, and the gain is in every stratum.
  • The design factor (experiment 7, 0.015 nats). The SD of the empirical null had been compensating for two separate things: the degrees of freedom and the variance inflation that donor-level covariates cost, which \(a_g\) and \(\nu\) now charge directly, and true weak effects, which had been inflating the null SD in the dense cells.
  • The log-scale estimator (experiment 12, 0.015 nats). The mean of log donor means is more efficient than the log of the mean because the bank’s donor effects are log-normal. This gain is the only large one that comes from the log fold change (the RMSE fell) and not from the SE.

The remaining kept commits are small. Experiments 8 and 15 cancel: the stored within-donor term acted as a general widening while the coverage was 0.944 and became redundant once the regression variance was in place. Experiments 9, 27 and 31 are each at about one paired SE, the level at which the keep rule admits a change with no effect about one time in six. Experiment 27 (the donor offset of step 3) is weakly tested by this bank, whose donors carry almost no depth error common to all genes.

Figure 4. The median standard error reported per test example, donor_wls against raw_null, by donor SD and covariates; the grey line marks equality.

The median SE of donor_wls is at or below that of raw_null in nearly every test example and varies less between examples of the same donor count, which is the effect of the moderation and of the removal of the cohort-wide null-SD factor.

The gain comes from how the variance is estimated and from the scale of the donor summary, in three steps: moderating the per-gene variance across genes, charging the donor-level covariates through the regression in place of the empirical null’s SD, and estimating the log fold change on the log scale. The other 12 kept commits add 0.011 nats together, and several of them are within the noise that the keep rule admits.

5 The withdrawn commits

The bank of Section 2, dev split. The SE diagnostics below were computed during the run on 12 dev cohorts by a script that was not kept, and are recorded in csv/RUN_nov11/validity.csv.

Table 4. The two commits that passed the keep rule and were withdrawn (gap_trend).
# Commit Direction Idea Gain Strata that moved
28 da743dc D4 Moderation trend against the arithmetic-geometric gap of the donor ratios 0.0248 every stratum (withdrawn)
29 b3fc556 D4 Variance as a direct smooth of that gap 0.0011 none individually (withdrawn)

gap_trend moderated the variance toward a trend in the gap between the log arithmetic mean and the mean log of a gene’s donor ratios, and it scored -0.1001 against -0.0742 for the commit before it. The gap is computed over all donors before the regression, so it contains the between-arm sum of squares, which is the squared estimated log fold change. With that covariate the prior degrees of freedom were infinite in every cohort checked, and the SE became a smooth function of the gap.

Table 5. Whether the reported SE follows the estimate, on 12 dev cohorts.
Rule Commit Median SE, strong-effect genes over the others Spearman correlation of SE and absolute logFC
gap_trend b3fc556 1.10 0.21
before the gap covariate 1de04e6 1.00 0.03
donor_wls 5df592c 0.98 0.01

Under gap_trend the SE of strong-effect genes was 1.10 times that of the other genes. The score rewards an SE that grows with the estimate because most true effects in the bank are near zero, so a gene with a large estimate is, on average, a gene with a large error. Such an SE is no longer the sampling SD of the log fold change, and it is the counterpart for the SE of the thresholding rule that the memo excludes for the log fold change. The gate examines only the slope of the log fold change, which gap_trend leaves unchanged.

Experiment 30 confirmed the mechanism: the same gap computed on the regression’s residuals, which do not contain the arm effect, scored -0.0150. Experiment 31 then replaced the kept covariate by one that is invariant to the arm effect, and the covariate of donor_wls gives a ratio of 0.98 and a correlation of 0.01.

On this bank the score pays 0.026 nats for an SE that depends on the estimated log fold change, and the gate on slope_weak does not detect it. The two commits were withdrawn by hand. A second gate, on the correlation between the reported SE and \(|\widehat\beta_g|\) or on the SE ratio of Table 5, would let the keep rule refuse such a commit.

The bank rewards D1, D2 and D4. The two D5 commits that were kept cancel each other (Section 4), and the three largest D5 losses share a cause: the fit’s case-control coefficient (experiment 11), its low-rank term (experiment 18) and its nuisance rate (experiment 24) are estimated at the level of cells, so they either weight donors by their cell count or absorb donor effects that the error of the log fold change still contains. Weighting donors by cell count directly (experiment 10) lost 0.056 nats for the same reason.

On D3 the empirical null’s mean is needed, since removing the centring (experiment 19) lost 0.036 nats, and none of four alternatives to the kept estimator of the centre improved on it. The SD of the empirical null could not be dropped before the design factor existed (experiments 1 and 6) and was dropped with it at experiment 7. The eighth item of the memo’s queue, a null SD fitted separately for capped and estimated genes, was therefore not run.

Quantities that eSVD-DE estimates at the level of cells did not improve a donor-level log fold change or its SE on this bank. donor_wls reads the counts, the design and the fitted library, and the fitted library is the only part of the fit it uses.

7 Constants

The truth was not on trial in this run. The kept commits introduced four numeric constants, and the dev split chose the value of none of them.

Constant Where Reason
1/2 half count in \(l_{dg}\) (step 1) continuity correction of a Poisson count, which keeps the logarithm finite at a zero count
0 floor of \(\tau^2\) and \(\phi\) (step 4) a variance component is not negative
50 iteration cap of the trigamma inverse (step 6) Newton’s method converges in under 10 steps, and the cap prevents an endless loop
\(10^{-8}\) convergence tolerance of the trigamma inverse (step 6) single precision in the relative step

The smoothness of the spline in step 6 is chosen by generalized cross-validation within each cohort.

8 Recommendation

Three statements follow from the evidence of this bank. donor_wls is the best rule the run found, and its gain holds on held-out examples (Section 3). The SD of the empirical null is not needed once the donor-level covariates are charged through the regression (Section 4). A gate on the dependence of the SE on the estimate is needed before another run (Section 5).

Three decisions are choices that the evidence does not settle, and they are Kevin’s: whether the withdrawal of gap_trend stands, whether the branch autoresearch_lfcse/nov11 is merged, and whether donor_wls replaces the earlier recommendation for compute_log_fold_change() before it has been checked on a second bank and on the real cohorts.

For one cohort fitted by eSVD() with the fitted library kept:

  1. Inputs. The counts, the fitted library library_mat, the design matrix, the donor of each cell and the arm of each cell.
  2. Check. Each arm has at least 5 donors, and \(n - q \ge 1\) after the donor-level covariates enter \(D\). The bank does not cover fewer than 5 donors per arm.
  3. Fit. report_lfc_se(view) of RULE_nov11_claude.R, which is donor_wls (Section 1.3, steps 1 to 8).
  4. Output. log2fc and se per gene. The Wald statistic is log2fc / se, referred to the standard normal distribution.
  5. Report alongside. The mean \(\delta_0\) of the empirical null and the shift \(\delta_0 \cdot \text{median}_g\, s_g\), the fitted \(\tau^2\) and \(\phi\), the prior degrees of freedom \(\nu_0\), and the Spearman correlation between se and the absolute log2fc.
  6. When to fall back. If that correlation is far from zero, or if the two arms differ visibly in the spread of their log donor means, the log fold change of donor_wls is a contrast of geometric means that need not equal the log ratio of mean expression (Section 9), and raw_null is reported beside it.

Three next experiments.

  1. An estimand check for the log-scale log fold change (D1; a new bank factor). The difference of mean log donor means equals the log ratio of mean expression only when the two arms have the same donor variance, which the bank imposes. A bank with unequal donor SD between the arms would show whether the gain of experiment 12 survives, or whether a correction of half the difference of the arms’ log-scale variances is needed.
  2. Donor-level depth error (D2; a new bank factor). The donor offset of step 3 is at one paired SE here because the bank’s donors carry no common depth error. A factor for that error would test the offset and whether the SE should then exclude that component.
  3. Capped genes (D5; a new bank). The bank caps 13% of genes at the wide rate range against 73% in the Velmeshev cohort, and the capped genes score 0.010 on test against -0.146 on dev. donor_wls no longer reads the nuisance rate, so the question is whether its SE stays calibrated when most genes are capped.

9 What we glossed over

  • The estimand. The log fold change of donor_wls is a contrast of geometric means over donors. It is taken up by the first next experiment of Section 8.
  • How much of eSVD-DE the rule needs. The contribution of the fitted library was not isolated, and the bank cannot reward the embedding (Section 1.3.2). A run of donor_wls with a plain library size, and a bank factor that confounds cell state with the arm, would settle both.
  • The package’s p-value was not on trial and still uses the posterior, so it can disagree with the Wald statistic of donor_wls (Section 1.3.2).
  • Keeps at one paired SE. Experiments 9, 27 and 31 cannot be separated from noise individually, and the test split scored only the final rule. A second bank (Section 8) would test the donor offset.
  • The SE diagnostics of Table 5 rest on 12 dev cohorts and a script that was not kept. The proposed gate (Section 5) would compute them for every example.
  • k_err and r_err, the errors in the two moments of Was2CoDE’s Figure 4, are omitted from Table 1. They are defined for about 80% of pairs and are dominated by a few near-zero denominators (BANK.md), so they are read by stratum in csv/RUN_nov11/scores.csv.
  • Real cohorts. No real cohort was read in this run. The exploration of 2026-11-07 (additional_context/2026-11-07_std-exploration/) holds the real-data checks that donor_wls has not yet been through.
  • The trial file’s header. The header comment of report_rule_claude.R at the best commit describes the rule as of experiment 15. The file was left as scored, and the header of RULE_nov11_claude.R is the accurate description.
